chunks: He said: Abu Hafs Umar ibn Muhammad al-Sayrafi reported to me from Abu al-Husayn al-Abbas ibn al-Mughairah al-Jawhari, who reported from Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi Abu Bakr, who reported from Ahmad ibn Salih, who reported from Anbasah, who reported from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Mukhramah al-Kindi who said:

Umar ibn al-Khattab went out one day and found himself at an assembly where Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), Uthman, Abd al-Rahman, Talha, and al-Zubayr were present. Umar said: 'Does every one of you aspire to leadership after me?' Al-Zubayr replied: 'Every one of us aspires to leadership after you and considers himself worthy of it. What is it that you disapprove?' Umar said: 'Shall I not tell you what I think about each of you?' They remained silent. Umar said: 'Shall I not tell you about yourselves?' They remained silent. Al-Zubayr said to him: 'Tell us, even if we remain silent.' Then he said: 'As for you, O Zubayr, you are a believer when pleased and a disbeliever when angry. One day you are a devil and another day a man. Tell me, on the day you are a devil, who will be the caliph then? And as for you, O Talha, by Allah, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) died while he was displeased with you. And as for you, O Ali, you are a man of inactivity and frivolity. And as for you, O Abd al-Rahman, by Allah, you are worthy of any good that comes your way. And indeed among you there is a man whose faith, if it were divided among armies, would suffice them all, and he is Uthman.'

key_terms.الخليفة: Caliph, successor to the Prophet in leading the Muslim community
key_terms.بطالة: Inactivity, idleness — used here as a derogatory characterization
key_terms.مزاح: Frivolity, jesting — used disparagingly about Ali

ai.seo_question: What did Umar ibn al-Khattab say about the companions regarding the caliphate?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Amali of al-Mufid records a historically significant exchange in which Umar ibn al-Khattab assessed the prominent companions regarding their fitness for the caliphate. In Shia scholarship, this account is notable because Umar's characterization of Imam Ali (AS) as a man of 'inactivity and frivolity' is seen as a deliberate attempt to undermine Ali's claim to leadership, while simultaneously elevating Uthman. The narration reveals the political dynamics among the companions during Umar's caliphate.
